rows.speaker: قراء المدينة والبصرة والشام وفقهاؤها
rows.claim: Medina, Basra, and Syrian readers and jurists hold that the basmala is not a verse of al-Fatiha or any surah.
rows.anchor: قرّاء المدينة والبصرة والشام وفقهاؤها على أنّ التسمية ليست بآية من الفاتحة ولا من غيرها من السور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It was written to separate surahs and seek blessing by beginning with it, as people begin important acts with it.
rows.anchor: وإنما كتبت للفصل والتبرك بالابتداء بها ، كما بدىء بذكرها في كل أمر ذي بال

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومن تابعه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and his followers share that position and therefore do not recite it aloud in prayer.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة - رحمه الله - ومن تابعه ، ولذلك لا يجهر بها عندهم في الصلاة

rows.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما
rows.claim: Meccan and Kufan readers and jurists, with al-Shafii and followers, count it as a verse of al-Fatiha and every surah.
rows.anchor: وقرّاء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما على أنها آية من الفاتحة ومن كل سورة ، وعليه الشافعي وأصحابه

rows.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما
rows.claim: Because they count it as a verse, this group recites it aloud in prayer.
rows.anchor: وعليه الشافعي وأصحابه رحمهم الله ، ولذلك يجهرون بها

rows.speaker: قراء مكة والكوفة وفقهاؤهما
rows.claim: Their proof is that early Muslims included it in the codex while requiring the Quran be stripped of additions, but omitted Amin.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : قد أثبتها السلف في المصحف مع توصيتهم بتجريد القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says whoever omits the basmala has omitted 114 verses of God's Book.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : «من تركها فقد ترك مائة وأربع عشرة آية من كتاب الله تعالى »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed bā attaches to an omitted verb, understood as I read or recite in God's name.
rows.anchor: بمحذوف تقديره : بسم الله اقرأ أو أتلو ؛ لأن الذي يتلو التسمية مقروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel formulas, slaughter, and acts begun in God's name similarly omit the verb that states the introduced act.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الذابح وكل فاعل يبدأ في فعله ؛ ب «بسم الله » كان مضمرا ما جعل التسمية مبدأ له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted governor in 27:12 is understood as go with nine signs to Pharaoh and his people.
rows.anchor: ونظيره في حذف متعلق الجار قوله عز وجل : { في تسع آيات إلى فرعون وقومه } [ النمل : 12 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wedding and blessing formulas omit a verb meaning you wed; the cited verse about going to food is another ellipsis example.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قول العرب في الدعاء للمعرس : بالرفاء والبنين ، وقول الأعرابي : باليمن والبركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted verb follows the basmala because God's name is the focus: fronting it gives exclusive force against beginning in idol names.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يبدءون بأسماء آلهتهم فيقولون : باسم اللات ، باسم العزى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This exclusivity resembles the fronted object in 1:5 and is supported by 11:41.
rows.anchor: وذلك بتقديمه وتأخير الفعل كما فعل في قوله : { إياك نعبد } ، حيث صرح بتقديم الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though 96:1 puts the verb first, there the command to read took precedence because it opened the first surah revealed.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : فقد قال : { اقرأ باسم ربك } [ العلق : 1 ] ، فقدّم الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes bā instrumental: a believer's act is not legally sound or in keeping with Sunna unless begun in God's name.
rows.anchor: في قولك : كتبت بالقلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The instrumental analysis invokes the Prophetic saying that an important matter begun without God's name is incomplete.
rows.anchor: كل أمر ذي بال لم يبدأ فيه باسم الله فهو أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other analysis makes bā mean accompaniment and blessing, as in a plant growing with oil; al-Zamakhshari calls this clearer and better.
rows.anchor: والثاني أن يتعلق بها تعلق الدهن بالإنبات في قوله : { تنبت بالدهن } [ المؤمنون : 20 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words are spoken on servants' tongues, as when one recites poetry for another; the Quran teaches blessing and praise.
rows.anchor: هذا مقول على ألسنة العباد ، كما يقول الرجل الشعر على لسان غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive lām is kasra to distinguish it from the emphatic lām; bā is kasra because it is inherently a particle governing the genitive.
rows.anchor: أما اللام فللفصل بينها وبين لام الابتداء ، وأما الباء فلكونها لازمة للحرفية والجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ism begins with a helping hamza initially because its first consonant is quiescent; in connected speech no addition is needed.
rows.anchor: والاسم أحد الأسماء العشرة التي بنوا أوائلها على السكون ، فإذا نطقوا بها مبتدئين زادوا همزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some omit the helping hamza and instead move the quiescent consonant, saying sim or sum.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من لم يزدها واستغنى عنها بتحريك الساكن ، فقال : سم وسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ism has a deleted ending like yad and dam; asma and sammaytu show its original sumu and derivation from elevation.
rows.anchor: وهو من الأسماء المحذوفة الأعجاز : كيد ودم ، وأصله : سمو ، بدليل تصريفه : كأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming raises the named one's standing; nabz derives from a word meaning raised voice and also means upper palm bark.
rows.anchor: لأن التسمية تنويه بالمسمى وإشادة بذكره ، ومنه قيل للقب النبز : من النبز بمعنى النبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written alif is dropped by analogy with connected pronunciation; the bā is lengthened to compensate for the omission.
rows.anchor: قد اتبعوا في حذفها حكم الدرج دون الابتداء الذي عليه وضع الخط لكثرة الاستعمال

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz told his scribe to lengthen bā, show tooth-like strokes, and round mīm.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه قال لكاتبه : طوّل الباء وأظهر السنات ودوّر الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah derives from al-ilah, with hamza removed; al-nas likewise derives from al-unas, with the hamza replaced by the article.
rows.anchor: قال : معاذ الإله أن تكون كظبيةٍ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the vocative, Allah keeps its hamza pronounced separately, as in ya ilah.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قيل في النداء : يا ألله بالقطع ، كما يقال : يا إله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilah is a common noun for anything worshipped truly or falsely, later restricted to the true deity, like words for star and house narrowed to the Pleiades and Kaaba.
rows.anchor: والإله من أسماء الأجناس كالرجل والفرس اسم يقع على كل معبود بحق أو باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah without hamza is uniquely the name of the true God and is never applied to another.
rows.anchor: فمختص بالمعبود بالحق ، لم يطلق على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'allaha, aliha, and ista'lah derive from this name, like verbs formed from camel and stone nouns.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا الاسم اشتق : تأله ، وأله ، واستأله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is a proper name, not an attribute; it is predicated of things but does not describe them, and divine attributes require a named subject.
rows.anchor: كما لا تقول : شيء رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible derivation links the name to aliha, be bewildered: minds are confounded by knowing God, helping explain error and scarce sound reflection.
rows.anchor: وصيغة قولهم : أله ، إذا تحير ، ومن أخواته : دله ، وعله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says emphatic pronunciation of Allah's lām is Sunna; Arabs all use it, showing inherited usage.
rows.anchor: قد ذكر الزجاج أن تفخيمها سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman follows faʿlan from rahima, like ghadban and sakran; rahim follows faʿil, like marid and saqim.
rows.anchor: غضبان وسكران ، من غضب وسكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is more intensive than rahim; tradition calls God Rahman of this world and the next, but Rahim of this world.
rows.anchor: رحمن الدنيا والآخرة ، ورحيم الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Added form means added meaning, illustrated by the heavier name shaqandaf for a light mount compared with shaqdaf.
rows.anchor: إن الزيادة في البناء لزيادة المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anecdote contrasts the light mount's name shaqdaf with shaqandaf, whose added letters express greater form.
rows.anchor: ومما طن على أذني من ملح العرب أنهم يسمون مركبا من مراكبهم بالشقدف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains ghadban as one filled with anger, illustrating the intensive pattern.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج في الغضبان : هو الممتلئ غضبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman is among dominant adjectival names that became proper names, like al-Dubaran and al-Ayyuq; Allah too is a dominant name.
rows.anchor: لم يستعمل في غير الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: بنو حنيفة وشاعرهم
rows.claim: Banu Hanifa called Musaylima Rahman of Yamama and their poet called him Rahman; al-Zamakhshari condemns this as unbelief.
rows.anchor: وأما قول بني حنيفة في مسيلمة : رحمان اليمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari declines Rahman without tanwin, by analogy with ghadban, gharthan, and sakran.
rows.anchor: أقيسه على أخواته من بابه ، أعني : نحو عطشان ، وغرثان ، وسكران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the usual diptote condition requires feminine faʿla, exclusivity does not remove the base pattern; faʿlana is also barred.
rows.anchor: فإذا لا عبرة بامتناع التأنيث للاختصاص العارض فوجب الرجوع إلى الأصل قبل الاختصاص وهو القياس على نظائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy suggests tenderness, as with a womb bending over its contents; of God it metaphorically means beneficence to servants, like a generous king.
rows.anchor: هو مجاز عن إنعامه على عباده ؛ لأن الملك إذا عطف على رعيته ورق لهم أصابهم بمعروفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman precedes rahim though the usual order rises from lesser to greater: it covers great foundational blessings, then rahim adds subtle ones.
rows.anchor: لما قال [ الرحمن ] فتناول جلائل النعم وعظائمها وأصولها ، أردفه ( الرحيم ) كالتتمة والرديف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd and madh are synonymous: praise for something beautiful, whether a blessing, good lineage, or courage.
rows.anchor: الحمد والمدح أخوان ، وهو الثناء والنداء على الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gratitude is for blessings and occurs by heart, tongue, and limbs; the poet names hand, tongue, and hidden conscience.
rows.anchor: أفادتكم النعماء مني ثلاثة *** يدي ولساني والضمير المحجبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamd is performed by the tongue alone and is one branch of gratitude.
rows.anchor: والحمد باللسان وحده ، فهو إحدى شعب الشكر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report calls praise the head of gratitude and says a servant has not thanked God without praising Him.
rows.anchor: الحمد رأس الشكر ، ما شكر الله عبد لم يحمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verbal praise publicizes a blessing and reveals awareness more clearly than hidden inward belief or ambiguous bodily acts.
rows.anchor: لأن ذكر النعمة باللسان والثناء على موليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise is opposite blame; gratitude is opposite ingratitude.
rows.anchor: والحمد نقيضه الذمّ ، والشكر نقيضه الكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hamdu is the subject and the prepositional phrase li-llah its predicate.
rows.anchor: وارتفاع الحمد بالابتداء وخبره الظرف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some readers use the accusative al-hamda, understood with an omitted verb.
rows.anchor: قراءة بعضهم بإضمار فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative treats hamd as a verbal noun with an omitted verb, as in shukran, kufran, and ajaban.
rows.anchor: المصادر التي تنصبها العرب بأفعال مضمرة في معنى الإخبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Subhanaka and maʿadha Allah stand in for their verbs, which speakers do not normally use alongside them.
rows.anchor: ينزلونها منزلة أفعالها ويسدون بها مسدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative instead of the accusative presents praise as established and lasting.
rows.anchor: والعدل بها عن النصب إلى الرفع على الابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 11:69 Abraham's nominative greeting signals more lasting peace than the visitors' accusative greeting.
rows.anchor: رفع السلام الثاني للدلالة على أن إبراهيم عليه السلام حياهم بتحية أحسن من تحيتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense is we praise God with praise; 1:5 explains the manner as worshipping and seeking help from Him.
rows.anchor: نحمد الله حمدا ، ولذلك قيل : { إياك نعبد وإياك نستعين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article marks generic praise, what everyone recognizes among kinds of acts; it does not signal exhaustive totality.
rows.anchor: هو تعريف الجنس ، ومعناه الإشارة إلى ما يعرفه كل أحد

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri reads the dāl with kasra by assimilation to the lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن البصري : { الحمد لله } بكسر الدال

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abi Abla reads the lām with damma by assimilation to the dāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة : { الحمد لله } بضم اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari prefers Ibrahim's reading because the stronger inflectional vowel controls the lexical vowel.
rows.anchor: حيث جعل الحركة البنائية تابعة للإعرابية التي هي أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb means owner; Safwan tells Abu Sufyan he prefers being owned by a Qurayshi to a Hawazini.
rows.anchor: قول صفوان لأبي سفيان : لأن يربني رجل من قريش أحب إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb may be an adjective formed from a verbal noun, expressing intensity like ʿadl.
rows.anchor: وصفا بالمصدر للمبالغة كما وصف بالعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unqualified rabb is only used of God; for others it is qualified, such as owner of a house or camel.
rows.anchor: ولم يطلقوا الرب إلا في الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quran examples use rabb relationally in 12:50 and 12:23.
rows.anchor: { ارجع إلى رَبِّكَ } [ يوسف : 50 ]

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads rabb al-alamin in the accusative as praise or an understood gloss of al-hamdu lillah.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله عنهما : { رب العالمين } بالنصب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-alam may mean beings with knowledge, angels and the two rational classes, humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: العالم : اسم لذوي العلم من الملائكة والثقلين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes al-alamin to mean everything the Creator knows, including bodies and accidents.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كل ما علم به الخالق من الأجسام والأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural includes every genus covered by the word.
rows.anchor: ليشمل كل جنس مما سمي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though alam is a noun, it can take the rational plural because it carries a descriptive sense of knowledge.
rows.anchor: ساغ ذلك لمعنى الوصفية فيه وهي الدلالة على معنى العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iya is a separate accusative pronoun; suffixes mark address, absence, and speaker without independent syntactic position.
rows.anchor: واللواحق التي تلحقه من الكاف والهاء والياء

rows.speaker: الأخفش والمحققون
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and careful grammarians hold that suffixes are not independent pronouns, like the kاف in araʾaytaka.
rows.anchor: وهو مذهب الأخفش وعليه المحققون

rows.speaker: الخليل وبعض العرب
rows.claim: Al-Khalil reports an anomalous expression using iya without a suffix, which al-Zamakhshari says should not be relied on.
rows.anchor: ما حكاه الخليل عن بعض العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting the object gives exclusive force, as in 39:64 and 6:164.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المفعول لقصد الاختصاص ، كقوله تعالى : { قل أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers devote worship and request help exclusively to God, seeking neither from anyone else.
rows.anchor: نخصك بالعبادة ، ونخصك بطلب المعونة .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading weakens the yā in iyaaka.
rows.anchor: وقريء :  "  إياك  "  بتخفيف الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has fatḥa on the hamza and a geminated yā.
rows.anchor: وأياك بفتح الهمزة والتشديد

rows.speaker: طفيل الغنوي
rows.claim: A reading changes initial hamza to hāʾ; Tufayl al-Ghanawi's verse witnesses hiyyaka.
rows.anchor: وهياك بقلب الهمزة هاء . قال طفيل الغنوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is utmost submission and abasement; related ʿabada describes thick, strongly woven cloth.
rows.anchor: والعبادة أقصى غاية الخضوع والتذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is reserved for God because He gives the greatest blessings and deserves highest submission.
rows.anchor: لأنه مولى أعظم النعم فكان حقيقا بأقصى غاية الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from third-person to address is iltifat; the Quran also shifts in 10:22 and 35:9.
rows.anchor: هذا يسمى الالتفات في علم البيان قد يكون من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: Imru al-Qays shifts perspective three times over three lines, illustrating varied discourse mode.
rows.anchor: وقد التفت امرؤ القيس ثلاث التفاتات في ثلاثة أبيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Changing discourse mode refreshes attention and awakens listening; this placement has additional benefits.
rows.anchor: ولأن الكلام إذا نقل من أسلوب إلى أسلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After praising God and listing His attributes, the speech directly addresses the one worthy of worship and help.
rows.anchor: تعلق العلم بمعلوم عظيم الشأن حقيق بالثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and help are paired to join what servants offer their Lord with what they request from Him.
rows.anchor: ليجمع بين ما يتقرب به العباد إلى ربهم وبين ما يطلبونه ويحتاجون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship comes before asking for help because offering the means before the request merits a response.
rows.anchor: تقديم الوسيلة قبل طلب الحاجة ليستوجبوا الإجابة إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking help is unqualified so it covers every matter in which help is needed.
rows.anchor: ليتناول كل مستعان فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Best is asking God and His enabling grace for help in worship; 1:6 specifies aid as guidance.
rows.anchor: والأحسن أن تراد الاستعانة به وبتوفيقه على أداء العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request for guidance explains what help is sought and coheres with the preceding words.
rows.anchor: ويكون قوله : { اهدنا } بيانا للمطلوب من المعونة

rows.speaker: ابن حبيش
rows.claim: Ibn Hubaysh reads nastaʿinu with kasra on its initial nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن حبيش :  "  نستعين  "  ، بكسر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hada normally takes li or ila, as in 17:9 and 42:52, but here takes a direct object by analogy with ikhtara in 7:155.
rows.anchor: هدى أصله أن يتعدى باللام أو بإلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Already guided worshippers ask for increased guidance through divine grace, as in 47:17 and 29:69.
rows.anchor: طلب زيادة الهدى بمنح الإلطاف

rows.speaker: علي وأبي
rows.claim: Ali and Ubayy explain ihdina as thabbitna, keep us firm.
rows.anchor: وعن علي وأبي رضي الله عنهما : اهدنا ثبتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imperative and supplicatory forms are alike because both request; they differ only in rank.
rows.anchor: وصيغة الأمر والدعاء واحدة ، لأن كل واحد منهما طلب

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah reads arshidna, guide us rightly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله : أرشدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat means the main road, named from swallowing because it swallows travelers, like luqman, the gulper.
rows.anchor: لأنه يسترط السابلة إذا سلكوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīn becomes ṣād before ṭā; ṣād can sound like zāy, but pure ṣād is the eloquent Qurayshi codex form.
rows.anchor: وقد تشم الصاد صوت الزاي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat has plural surut, like kitab and kutub, and can be masculine or feminine like tariq and sabil.
rows.anchor: ويجمع سرطا ، نحو كتاب وكتب ، ويذكر ويؤنث كالطريق والسبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the path of truth, the religion of Islam.
rows.anchor: والمراد طريق الحق وهو ملة الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirat alladhina is appositive to the straight path and repeats the request for guidance.
rows.anchor: وهو في حكم تكرير العامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apposition reinforces and explains the straight path as the Muslims' path, certifying its uprightness emphatically.
rows.anchor: فائدته التوكيد لما فيه من التثنية والتكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those blessed are the believers.
rows.anchor: والذين أنعمت عليهم : هم المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is general to include every blessing; whoever receives Islam receives every blessing.
rows.anchor: من أنعم عليه بنعمة الإسلام لم تبق نعمة إلا أصابته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as Moses's companions before they changed.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : هم أصحاب موسى قبل أن يغيروا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as the prophets.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads sirat man anʿamta ʿalayhim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «صراط من أنعمت عليهم »

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr can be appositive to those blessed, meaning they are spared God's anger and error.
rows.anchor: بدل من الذين أنعمت عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ghayr is an adjective: the blessed combine faith with safety from anger and error.
rows.anchor: أو صفة على معنى أنهم جمعوا بين النعمة المطلقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr can modify the definite relative phrase because it is undelimited and the angry and astray are opposites of the blessed.
rows.anchor: قلت : { الذين أنعمت عليهم } لا توقيت فيه

rows.speaker: النبي وعمر بن الخطاب وابن كثير
rows.claim: The accusative ghayra is a circumstantial reading attributed to the Prophet, Umar, and Ibn Kathir.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who incurred anger are identified as Jews, with 5:60 cited.
rows.anchor: المغضوب عليهم : هم اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those astray are identified as Christians, with 5:77 cited.
rows.anchor: والضالون : هم النصارى ؛ لقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's anger is His will to avenge sinners and punish them, acting as a king does when angry with a subordinate.
rows.anchor: هو إرادة الانتقام من العصاة ، وإنزال العقوبة بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ʿalayhim is accusative as object of anʿamta; the second is nominative as agent in the passive phrase.
rows.anchor: الأولى محلها النصب على المفعولية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La appears because ghayr already carries negation: neither the angered nor the astray.
rows.anchor: لما في غير من معنى النفي

rows.speaker: عمر وعلي
rows.claim: Umar and Ali read wa-ghayr al-dallin.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر وعلي رضي الله عنهما أنهما قرآ : وغير الضالين

rows.speaker: أيوب السختياني
rows.claim: Ayyub reads with hamza; Amr ibn Ubayd also uses a hamza form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أيوب السختياني : «ولا الضألين » بالهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: The hamza dialect avoids meeting two quiescent consonants, as in Abu Zayd's shaʾba and daʾba.
rows.anchor: وهذه لغة من جد في الهرب من التقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin is a sound-form used as the name of the verb respond, like words meaning wait, hurry, and come.
rows.anchor: صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والنبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas asked the Prophet what Amin means, and the Prophet answered, do it.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin has long and short alif, both attested by poetry.
rows.anchor: وفيه لغتان : مد ألفه ، وقصرها

rows.speaker: النبي وجبريل
rows.claim: Gabriel taught the Prophet Amin at the end of al-Fatiha and called it a seal on a book.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : "  لقنني جبريل عليه السلام آمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amin is not Quran because it was not entered in the codices.
rows.anchor: وليس من القرآن بدليل أنه لم يثبت في المصاحف

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the imam should not say Amin because the imam is the supplicant.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن : لا يقولها الإمام لأنه الداعي

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa is reported to say the imam should not say Amin.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رحمه الله مثله

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: The well-known position of Abu Hanifa and his followers is to say Amin silently.
rows.anchor: والمشهور عنه وعن أصحابه أنه يخفيها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل وأنس والنبي
rows.claim: Silent recitation is reported from the Prophet by Abdullah ibn Mughaffal and Anas.
rows.anchor: وروى الإخفاء عبد الله بن مغفل وأنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafii holds Amin is said aloud.
rows.anchor: وعند الشافعي يجهر بها

rows.speaker: وائل بن حجر والنبي
rows.claim: Waʾil ibn Hujr reports that the Prophet said Amin aloud after wa-la al-dallin.
rows.anchor: وعن وائل بن حجرأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ : ولا الضالين

rows.speaker: النبي وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: The Prophet says al-Fatiha has no equal in the Torah, Gospel, or Quran and is the seven oft-repeated verses and great Quran given to him.
rows.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبيّ بن كعب

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان والنبي
rows.claim: Hudhayfa reports that when a child recites al-Fatiha amid certain punishment, God hears and lifts it for forty years.
rows.anchor: وعن حذيفة بن اليمان أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ala is Meccan and consists of nineteen verses.
rows.anchor:
مقدمة السورة:
مكية وآياتها 19

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God's name declares Him free of heretical meanings attributed to His names, such as determinism or anthropomorphism.
rows.anchor: تنزيهه عما لا يصح فيه من المعاني التي هي إلحاد في أسمائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ala is exalted in domination and power, not spatial height or literal establishment on the Throne.
rows.anchor: مثل أن يفسر الأعلى بمعنى العلو الذي هو القهر والاقتدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's name is protected from casual mention and spoken with humility and reverence.
rows.anchor: وأن يصان عن الابتذال والذكر ، لا على وجه الخشوع والتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ala may be parsed as an adjective of rabb.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { الأعلى } صفة للرب

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reads Subhana rabbi al-aʿla instead of sabbih.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي رضي الله عنه : سبحان ربي الأعلى

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet directs the command to glorify the great Lord by name for bowing, and this verse for prostration.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : "  اجعلوها في ركوعكم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says to place this glorification in prostration.
rows.anchor: فلما نزل سبح اسم ربك الأعلى قال : "  اجعلوها في سجودكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their formulas were, in bowing, God, to You I bow, and in prostration, God, to You I prostrate.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يقولون في الركوع : اللهم لك ركعت ، وفي السجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nar al-kubra is the lowest layer among Hell's layers.
rows.anchor: { النار الكبرى } السفلى من أطباق النار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies al-kubra as Jahannam.
rows.anchor: وقيل { الكبرى } نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesser fire is the fire of this world.
rows.anchor: والصغرى نار الدنيا
